sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Death of Moderates**: The passing of **G.K. Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta** in 1915 removed the primary ideological roadblocks to reconciliation.
• **Home Rule Momentum**: The **Home Rule Leagues** (Tilak and Besant) necessitated a unified platform to exert pressure on the British government during WWI.
• **Changing Global Context**: The **First World War** created a sense of urgency for unity to demand constitutional reforms (Self-Government).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** served as the institutional bridge, reconciling not just the factions of Congress, but also the Congress and the Muslim League.

items.definition: An agreement between INC and Muslim League; facilitated by Tilak and Jinnah, it provided a unified front for the readmission of extremists.
A political movement led by Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak that acted as the catalyst for bringing the two factions together under a common goal.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Unified Congress**: The 1916 session marked the end of the 'Surat Split' era.
• **Joint Demand**: Congress and Muslim League presented a joint scheme for constitutional reforms.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Ideological differences remained; the unity was tactical rather than permanent.
• **Solutions**: The emergence of Gandhi in 1917-18 provided a new, non-factional leadership.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-U-H' (Deaths, Unity, Home Rule).
• **Decoded Meaning**: **D**eaths of Gokhale/Mehta, **U**nity of Congress-League, **H**ome Rule Movement pressure.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Lucknow Pact' (Congress-League) with the 'Readmission of Extremists' (Congress-Congress). Both happened in 1916, but they are distinct political events.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Tactical Reconciliation' to describe the 1916 unity, noting that it was driven by external pressures rather than total ideological convergence.

keyTakeaways: The death of moderate stalwarts removed the primary barrier to re-entry.
The Home Rule Movement provided the necessary organizational pressure for unity.
The 1916 Lucknow Session is the landmark event for both Congress unity and the Congress-League Pact.
